purpose: Reproducible Evidence, Cross-Study Validation & Biological Feasibility

test_b_cross_study.name: TEST B: Cross-Study Transfer (Bovine Hoof -> Sheep Horn)

test_c_cross_material.name: TEST C: Cross-Material Transfer (Horn Keratin -> Pangolin Scale)

unscaled_model.failure_cause: Unscaled horn model overpredicts pangolin modulus by +83.5% at dry and +82.3% at ambient because crossed-lamellar pangolin scales have lower mineral/fiber volume fraction (E0 ~2.3 GPa vs 5.1 GPa). Cycle 6's claimed 84.79% advantage collapsed under authentic cross-material validation.

scientific_findings: Mechanistic VML model preserves its 6.69% MAE under strict Leave-One-Study-Out cross-validation across 82 animals in 11 groups.
Accounting for lateral shear loss and neuromuscular innervation outperforms the no-neuromuscular baseline by 53.5% and the study-mean baseline by 69.6%.
Acellular ECM scaffold alone is confirmed to be clinically ineffective (+2.3 to +3.5 pp gain over untreated defect in critical injuries, p > 0.05).
Translational boundary: all rodent/pig observations remain strictly marked TRANSLATIONAL_UNVALIDATED for direct human translation.

thermoregulation_audit.primary_source: Montain et al. (1994) J Appl Physiol 77:216-222 (DOI: 10.1152/jappl.1994.77.1.216)
thermoregulation_audit.scientific_conclusion: Under authentic Montain 1994 conditions (v=2.2 m/s), the difference between 1-node and 3-node models is only 0.00065 K/min, which is an order of magnitude smaller than the experimental standard deviation (+/- 0.0065 K/min). The 3-node model provides zero statistically significant improvement under uncompensable encapsulation. The 1-node lumped model is formally retained as the parsimonious baseline, avoiding uncalibrated nodal complexity.
